The Mechanistic Toxicology Branch (MTB) within the DTT conducts laboratory research to identify human health hazards and understand environmental toxicity through hybrid basic and applied science approaches that include development of new approach methods (NAMs) for toxicology research. The MTB is pioneering innovative toxicology research with advanced cell systems such as human tissue chips and 3D organoid models to understand the adverse effects of chemicals, drugs, and natural products and develop innovative solutions for translational toxicology research. 2) Objectives: The MTB seeks to solve ongoing challenges in the scalable generation of 3D human organoid/spheroid models by exploring the potential of microencapsulation technology to bioengineer human tissue models that better reflect human physiology for translational toxicology research. A Fluigent Microencapsulation System has been identified as uniquely suited for our exploratory research needs to model toxicity-induced liver fibrosis with 3D microtissue models.
